# Moving Content: One Visible at a Time

#### Course: Make Your Website Interactive with JavaScript

## Moving Content: One Visible at a Time

You already know how state controls what the user sees.

Now let's apply that to something you will actually use in your portfolio — a slider.

A slider shows several items in a row, but only one or a fixed set is visible at a time. The rest are still there, just outside the visible area.

All slides sit inside a track. The outer container hides anything that overflows. When the track moves left or right, a different slide comes into view.

![Moving Content: One Visible at a Time](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

You can control this in two common ways:

- Move the container using marginLeft or transform
- Show and hide items using classes

To know which slide should appear, we store one value in a variable:

```javascriptDOM
var currentSlideIndex = 0;
```

This number represents the position of the active slide.

When the index changes, we update the container's position or apply the correct class so the right slide becomes visible.

It follows the same state pattern:

- Update the variable first
- Then update the DOM to match it

Next, you will see a runnable example where the track moves based on this index.
